body.proof_tex:
Fix an admissible path \(P_t\) and write \(r_t=dP_t/dP\) and \(z_t=\sqrt{r_t}-1\).  By DQM, \(z_t=ts/2+o_{L^2(P)}(t)\), and hence \(\|z_t\|_2=O(|t|)\).  The likelihood-ratio ball in \(\mathrm{def:local-operator-chart}\), together with \(0<\varepsilon<1\), bounds \(r_t\) above and away from zero, so \(\sup_t\|z_t\|_\infty<\infty\) locally.  Therefore every fixed \(f\in L^2(P)\) satisfies
\[
 E_{P_t}f-E_Pf
 =E_P\{f(2z_t+z_t^2)\}
 =tE_P(fs)+o(t).
\]
Indeed, the linear term follows by Cauchy--Schwarz.  For the quadratic term, for every \(M>0\),
\[
 \frac{E_P(|f|z_t^2)}{|t|}
 \le M\frac{\|z_t\|_2^2}{|t|}
 +\|f\mathbf 1\{|f|>M\}\|_2
   \frac{\|z_t\|_\infty\|z_t\|_2}{|t|}.
\]
The first term tends to zero for fixed \(M\), the second has limsup bounded by a constant times \(\|f\mathbf 1\{|f|>M\}\|_2\), and this last norm tends to zero as \(M\to\infty\).  Thus the displayed expectation derivative is justified without assuming bounded bridges.

Put \(B_{h,q}=\sum_{a=0}^1t_aS_a(h_a,q_a)=\theta(P)+\phi_{h,q}\).  The base score is square-integrable by hypothesis, so the preceding calculation gives
\[
 E_{P_t}B_{h,q}-E_PB_{h,q}
 =tE_P(\phi_{h,q}s)+o(t),
\]
where \(E_Ps=0\) removes the centering constant.  It remains to compare \(E_{P_t}B_{h,q}\) with \(\theta(P_t)\).  First, the arm mean does not depend on the selected outcome bridge: if \(h_{a,t}'\) is another solution, then \(u=h_{a,t}'-h_{a,t}\in\ker T_{a,t}\), and any \(q_{a,t}\in\mathcal Q_a(P_t)\) gives
\[
 E_{P_t}u=E_{P_t}(I_aq_{a,t}u)
 =E_{P_t}\{I_aq_{a,t}T_{a,t}u\}=0.
\]
All products are integrable by Cauchy--Schwarz and the square-integrability of the two bridges under \(P_t\).  Thus \(\theta_a(P_t)=E_{P_t}h_{a,t}\) is well defined.  For one arm, outcome-bridge solvability under \(P_t\) gives
\[
 E_{P_t}\!\left[I_aq_a\{Y-h_{a,t}(W,X)\}\right]=0,
\]
because \(q_a\) is a function of \((Z,X)\) and \(E_{P_t}[Y-h_{a,t}(W,X)\mid A=a,Z,X]=0\).  Treatment-bridge solvability under \(P_t\) gives
\[
 E_{P_t}\!\left[(1-I_aq_{a,t})\{h_{a,t}(W,X)-h_a(W,X)\}\right]=0.
\]
Subtracting these two identities from the definition of \(S_a\) yields the exact mixed-bias identity
\[
 \theta_a(P_t)-E_{P_t}S_a(h_a,q_a)
 =E_{P_t}\!\left[I_a(q_{a,t}-q_a)(h_{a,t}-h_a)\right],
 \qquad \theta_a(P_t)=E_{P_t}h_{a,t}.
\]
Conditioning first on \((A,Z,X)\), or first on \((W,X)\), and applying Cauchy--Schwarz gives respectively
\[
 \left|\theta_a(P_t)-E_{P_t}S_a(h_a,q_a)\right|
 \le
 \|T_{a,t}(h_{a,t}-h_a)\|_{\mathcal G_a(P_t)}
 \|q_{a,t}-q_a\|_{\mathcal G_a(P_t)}
\]
and
\[
 \left|\theta_a(P_t)-E_{P_t}S_a(h_a,q_a)\right|
 \le
 \|h_{a,t}-h_a\|_{\mathcal H(P_t)}
 \|T_{a,t}^*(q_{a,t}-q_a)\|_{\mathcal H(P_t)}.
\]
The assumed minimum of these products is \(o(|t|)\) in each arm.  Taking the signed arm difference proves
\[
 \theta(P_t)-\theta(P)=tE_P(\phi_{h,q}s)+o(t).
\]
Thus \(\phi_{h,q}\) is a gradient on the actual score set, and continuity extends the representation to \(\mathcal T_P\).

By \(\mathrm{lem:normal-affine-identity}\), \(\mathcal A_P=\phi_0+\mathcal C_P\).  The point
\[
 \phi_* =\phi_0-\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0,
 \qquad \phi_*\perp\mathcal C_P.
\]
belongs to \(\phi_0+\mathcal C_P\).  For every \(c\in\mathcal C_P\), orthogonality gives
\[
 \|\phi_0+c\|_2^2
 =\|\phi_*\|_2^2+\|\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0+c\|_2^2,
\]
so \(\phi_*\) is the unique minimum-norm point.
The assumed tangent equality makes \(\phi_*\in\mathcal T_P\).  For \(v\in\mathcal T_P\),
\[
 E(\phi_*v)=E(\phi_0v)-E\{(\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0)v\}=\dot\theta_P(v),
\]
so \(\phi_*\) is the canonical gradient.  If \(g\in L_0^2(P)\) is any other gradient, then \(g-\phi_0\in\mathcal T_P^\perp=\mathcal C_P\); conversely, every \(\phi_0+c\), \(c\in\mathcal C_P\), represents the same derivative.  Hence the gradient set is exactly \(\mathcal A_P\), and minimizing its squared norm proves both asserted formulas.  None of these steps proves that an arbitrary Riesz representer must be an individual bridge-pair score, which is why no converse is claimed.
body.justification: The Hilbert projection and complete gradient-affine-space calculation are proved once tangent equality and bridge-score pathwise validity are available.
body.gap: Neither reverse score lifting nor unbounded-product bridge-score validity, including the claimed necessity of \(\Phi_P\ne\varnothing\), follows from the frozen assumptions.
body.consumer: Analysts must use the unconditional positive finite results or state both missing premises explicitly.
